decisions.context: Forecasts must be reproducible for any past week, including their inputs and training context. The team needs a way to track experiments and production artifacts.
decisions.rationale: It covers dataset versions, pipeline definitions, dependencies, and training snapshots needed to reproduce a past forecast. “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” and “MLOps Principles” support this traceability approach.
consequences: Retain versioned inputs and training context.
Budget effort for metadata and artifact management.

decisions.context: A scheduled weekly forecast needs repeatable stages that can run without hand-coordinated transitions. New model ideas should fit into the same workflow.
decisions.rationale: A pipeline makes weekly preparation, training, evaluation, and promotion repeatable while providing a path for new candidates. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” describe this approach; the manual workflow is described as suitable for infrequently changing models in “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture.”
consequences: Make the weekly run observable and restartable.
Choose a data-ingestion mechanism before finalizing orchestration; the design-space point flags this dependency.

decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly without breaking the scheduled weekly forecast. Releases need a way to limit impact and recover.
decisions.rationale: Incremental promotion and rollback directly address the risk of a new model disrupting the weekly run. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” support this release pattern.
consequences: Keep a known-good model available for recovery.
Add staged promotion to the release path.
Automate rollback or document its operational trigger.

decisions.context: Candidates need to be evaluated before replacing the production model, with checks that detect deterioration. The brief does not specify a particular forecasting metric or threshold.
decisions.rationale: Offline evaluation provides the pre-promotion comparison needed to introduce new model ideas safely. “MLOps Principles” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” support held-out evaluation; metric and threshold selection remain system-specific.
consequences: Preserve evaluation data and results for comparison.
Define forecasting metrics and acceptance thresholds separately.

decisions.context: Reproducing a forecast from a past week requires retaining its input data and provenance. The brief does not state retention or privacy constraints.
decisions.rationale: Keeping inputs recoverable with their provenance supports replaying forecasts from past weeks. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” and “Architecting a Machine Learning System for Risk” support preservation and traceability.
consequences: Retain source snapshots or equivalent immutable inputs.
Record processing provenance for each forecast run.

uncovered: Data-ingestion mechanism and source-system interfaces; the checked design point says workflow coordination requires this decision first.
Forecasting model family and business-selected error metric or acceptance thresholds.
Weekly schedule, late-data handling, and rerun policy.
Data-retention duration, access controls, and privacy constraints.
Production monitoring signals and alert ownership.
